ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A simple pendulum has a length of $L = 10\mathrm{m}$. When the pendulum undergoes small-angle oscillations (with an angle less than $5^{\circ}$), and air resistance is neglected, the gravitational acceleration is $g = 10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. Find the oscillation period of the simple pendulum.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A simple pendulum has a length of $L = 10\mathrm{m}$. When the pendulum undergoes small-angle oscillations (with an angle less than $5^{\circ}$), and air resistance is neglected, the gravitational acceleration is $g = 10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$. 1. Find the oscillation period of the simple pendulum.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The problem gives a simple pendulum of length L = 10 m and gravitational acceleration g = 10 m/s^2. The oscillation angle is less than 5°, so the small-angle approximation applies, and air resistance is neglected. For a small-angle simple pendulum, the period is T = 2π√(L/g). Substituting the given values gives T = 2π√(10/10) = 2π√1 = 2π s.
